whyPlan.title: Why plan?
whyPlan.subtitle: Before the 'what' and the 'how', the why. See what changes when money has a plan.

c1.q: I already invest. Why do I need a plan?
c1.a: Investing without a plan is having the pieces without the puzzle. A plan gives every real a job: a goal, a horizon and a fitting risk. Without it, a portfolio can look 'good' — and still not take you where you want to go.

c2.q: Why talk about my life before talking about products?
c2.a: A product is the 'what'. Your life is the 'why'. Without the why, any product fits — and none solves it. The plan is born from your goals; products are a consequence.

c3.q: What happens if I don't plan?
c3.a: The short term decides for you: surprises become debt, retirement gets postponed, and succession turns into cost and family conflict — at the worst possible time.

c4.q: Why start now and not next year?
c4.a: Time is the only asset you can't get back. Every year delayed needs a bigger monthly contribution for the same goal.

duration.title: How long income lasts
duration.body: How many years the portfolio sustains the retirement income need before depleting.

probability.title: Probability of success
probability.body: Chance the plan funds the desired income across the whole horizon — capital at retirement vs. capital needed.

estate.title: Estate at horizon
estate.body: How much should remain at the end of the planning horizon (legacy / margin).

gap.title: Retirement income gap
gap.body: The gap between the portfolio's sustainable monthly income IN RETIREMENT and the desired income. Not the same as free balance — today's monthly surplus to invest. Negative = shortfall; positive = surplus.

goals.title: Goals
goals.body: How many goals are achievable in the current scenario. Tap each one for detail.

why.succession: A sizeable estate needs succession and liquidity planning.
why.autoInvest: Monthly surplus not yet automated into investments.
why.medicalContinuity: High recurring medical costs with dependents — fund the stream and secure coverage continuity.
why.incomeLadder: Approaching retirement — convert the portfolio into an inflation-protected income stream.
why.inflowParking: Sizable inflow expected in {ano} — deciding its destination before the money lands avoids idle cash.
why.inflowSuccession: The inflow expected in {ano} is the opportunity to fund the succession liquidity still missing.
why.plannedSavings: Event planned for {ano}: a contribution of {aporte, number, ::currency/BRL}/month gets there without credit.
why.plannedFinancing: The {ano} event is close and the required contribution ({aporte, number, ::currency/BRL}/month) does not fit the surplus — structured financing/consortium preserves the plan.
why.educationHorizon: Education with a {anos}-year horizon until {ano} — long horizons favor instruments with long-term benefits (attributes, not labels).
why.businessVolatility: Opening a business in {ano} makes income more volatile — review life/disability coverage BEFORE the move.
why.travelFx: Relevant international expense in {ano} — programming FX dilutes rate risk.
why.familyGrowing: Family growing in {ano} — protection and planning must keep up.
why.decumulation: Outflow planned for {ano}, already in the usufruct phase — review the income plan.
why.decumulationDepletes: The outflow planned for {ano} happens in retirement and wealth depletes in {anoEsgotamento} — review decumulation/programmed income.
why.depletionPlan: On the current path wealth depletes in {anoEsgotamento} — structuring lifetime income/pension protects longevity.
why.goalGap: Goal underfunded until {ano} — a programmed contribution of {aporte, number, ::currency/BRL}/month closes the gap.
why.tooRisky: Conservative profile with a risk-heavy allocation — realign the portfolio to suitability.
why.tooConservative: Aggressive profile with excess cash — the money is below the client mandate.
why.ownershipConcentration: Wealth concentrated in a single holder with an active succession goal — structure the succession plan.
